fictional_notice: FICTIONAL SYNTHETIC DATA. NOT A REAL PATIENT.
text:
Nursing Event Note, 2034-01-31

At 14:52, while I was in the room, the patient had a generalized tonic-clonic seizure lasting about 50 seconds, which stopped on its own. The patient was turned on the side, oxygen was applied, and the rapid response team was called; no benzodiazepine was needed because the seizure had already ended. Vital signs afterwards: heart rate 118, blood pressure 132/80, oxygen saturation 98% on 2 L.

By 15:20 the patient was awake and answering questions. ICE at 15:25 was 7/10: the patient did not know the month or the name of the hospital and could not write a sentence, but named all objects, followed the command and counted correctly. There was a small bite mark on the left side of the tongue.
